title: Baked Salmon with Fresh Lemon and Dill

source.name: 7 Nutrient-Packed Recipes That Make Healthy Eating a Breeze - Prime Women
source.location: Baked Salmon with Lemon and Dill Section

ingredients.name: sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper

steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
Arrange the salmon fillets skin-side down on the prepared baking sheet with space between them.
Drizzle fillets evenly with olive oil, and season generously with sea salt and cracked black pepper.
Top each fillet with fresh lemon slices and fresh dill sprigs.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the salmon is opaque, flakes easily with a fork, and reaches 145°F internal temperature.
Serve warm with the roasted lemon slices.
swaps: Can substitute lime slices and cilantro for a Mexican flavor profile; skinless fillets work equally well.
notes: Minimalist Mediterranean preparation that lets fresh salmon flavor shine without added heavy fats.

title: Sheet-Pan Chili-Lemon Salmon and Potatoes

source.name: Healthy Weeknight Dinners You'll Actually Crave - Dishing Out Health

ingredients.name: baby Yukon gold potatoes, halved or quartered

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C). Toss halved potatoes with 1.5 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 15 minutes until they begin to brown and turn tender when pierced.
Meanwhile, in a small dish, whisk together remaining olive oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Push roasted potatoes to one side of sheet pan. Arrange salmon fillets and trimmed asparagus spears on the remaining space.
Brush chili-lemon mixture generously over salmon and asparagus.
Return sheet pan to oven and roast for 12 to 14 minutes until salmon flakes tenderly and asparagus is crisp-tender.
swaps: Can use sweet potato cubes instead of baby Yukon golds; green beans work well in place of asparagus.
notes: Staggering the cooking times ensures potatoes get crispy without overcooking the salmon.

title: Skillet Salmon with Creamy Spinach and Artichokes

source.name: Healthy Weeknight Dinners You'll Actually Crave - Dishing Out Health

ingredients.name: heavy cream or culinary coconut cream

steps: Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear salmon for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown; transfer to a plate (salmon will finish cooking in sauce).
Lower skillet heat to medium, add minced garlic and chopped artichoke hearts, sautéing for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in broth and cream, bringing to a gentle simmer for 2 minutes.
Add fresh spinach and parmesan, stirring until spinach wilts into the creamy sauce.
Return seared salmon fillets to skillet, spooning sauce over top, and simmer for 3 minutes until salmon flakes tenderly.
swaps: Can add chopped sun-dried tomatoes; Greek cream cheese or coconut cream can lighten the sauce.
notes: Rich bistro-style skillet dinner that comes together in one pan in 30 minutes.

title: Classic Miso-Glazed Broiled Salmon

source.name: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

steps: In a small bowl, whisk together white miso paste, mirin, soy sauce, honey, and grated ginger until smooth.
Place salmon fillets in a shallow dish, brush glaze generously over flesh, and let marinate for 15 minutes.
Line a baking sheet with foil and lightly grease with oil. Arrange salmon fillets skin-side down on foil.
Position oven rack 5 inches below the broiler and turn on high broil.
Broil salmon for 6 to 8 minutes without flipping, watching carefully as the miso glaze caramelizes and bubbles into deep golden-brown spots.
Remove when edges are caramelized and fish flakes easily; garnish with sliced scallions and serve with steamed rice.
swaps: Can substitute red miso paste for a bolder savory taste; maple syrup can replace honey.
notes: Inspired by the classic Nobu-style preparation. Watch closely under the broiler to prevent sugars from burning.

title: Crispy Skin Pan-Roasted Salmon with Lemon & Capers

source.name: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

ingredients.name: neutral high-heat oil (avocado or light olive oil)
kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper

steps: Use paper towels to pat the salmon skin completely dry. Lightly score skin with 3 shallow diagonal cuts and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy cast-iron or stainless steel skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place fillets skin-side down in pan. Press gently with a flat spatula for 30 seconds to prevent the skin from curling.
Cook undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes until skin is deeply golden, crisp, and releases easily from the pan.
Carefully flip fillets and cook on flesh side for 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove pan from heat; add butter, capers, lemon juice, and parsley, swirling the pan so melted butter foams and creates a pan sauce.
Spoon foaming lemon-caper butter over salmon flesh and serve immediately with skin facing up.
swaps: Can use olive oil only for a dairy-free piccata sauce; add a splash of dry white wine with lemon juice.
notes: The essential technique for restaurant-grade crackling skin: bone-dry skin and initial spatula pressure.

title: Honey-Mustard Glazed Baked Salmon

source.name: 45 Healthy Comfort Food Recipes - Food Network

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C) and line a baking sheet with foil.
In a small ramekin, whisk together Dijon mustard, whole grain mustard, honey, minced garlic, lemon juice, and smoked paprika.
Arrange salmon fillets skin-side down on the prepared baking sheet and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Spoon honey-mustard glaze evenly across the top of each fillet, spreading to the edges.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until salmon is cooked through and glaze is bubbling and caramelized.
Serve hot alongside roasted vegetables or steamed brown rice.
swaps: Maple syrup can substitute for honey; spicy brown mustard can replace whole grain mustard.
notes: Sweet and tangy glaze keeps lean salmon succulent during high-heat roasting.

title: Cast-Iron Blackened Cajun Salmon

source.name: Our 50 Most-Popular Healthy Recipes - Food Network

steps: In a small dish, mix smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, thyme, cayenne, salt, and black pepper into a Cajun spice rub.
Brush salmon fillets on all sides with melted butter or oil, then coat flesh liberally with the spice rub.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot.
Place fillets flesh-side down in dry or lightly oiled hot skillet; sear undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes until a dark, flavorful, blackened crust forms.
Flip fillets and cook for another 3 minutes until salmon is just cooked through.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges for squeezing over the crust.
swaps: Can use store-bought Cajun or Creole blackened seasoning mix; reduce cayenne for milder spice.
notes: Authentic blackened crust without deep frying. Ensure kitchen is well ventilated as searing spices produces aromatic smoke.
